title: Is 17 really the average of this dot plot?
description: A question from the book shows a dot plot with some values repeated and asks whether seventeen is its average. The video counts the dots, adds the values with their repeats, divides to get the mean, and checks by adding the distances on each side of seventeen.
teaching_notes: One idea: a repeated value counts once for each dot, so the sum and the count both include every dot. Watch for students who add each distinct value once and divide by the number of different values.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 7)
video_script.why: The child can guess that the tallest stack is the average, but only the sum and the count, or the balance of distances, can settle it.
video_script.substitution: Count every dot, add every value with its repeats, divide, and check that the distances from seventeen do not balance.
video_script.anchor: a dot plot on a number line from fourteen to twenty three, with stacks of dots and a marker at seventeen
video_script.payoff_line: No, the mean is seventeen point seven two

final_answer.spoken: no, the mean is seventeen point seven two

never_show: the mean 17.72 before the answer beat
video_script.design: One idea: count and add every dot, then divide. The dot plot stays from ground to the end of the idea part.
open_questions: The dot counts come from the worklist; the book figure is not in the extracted text.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a dot plot.

narration: <bookmark mark='stacks'/>We use the same way as the example in your book. Every dot is one value.
<bookmark mark='repeat'/>A value with three dots counts three times, in the sum and in the count.

beats.on_screen: Given: dots 2 at 14, 2 at 15, 3 at 16, 5 at 17, 4 at 18, 4 at 19, 3 at 20, 1 at 21, 1 at 23

marks.given: the dots of each stack are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a dot plot with a stack of dots at each value from fourteen to twenty three.

beats.on_screen: To find: whether 17 is the average of the data

marks.find: the thing to find is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find whether seventeen is the average of the data.

marks.count: the dots of the stacks are added: 2 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 25

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step one, the count. Adding the dots of all the stacks gives twenty five dots.

marks.times: each value is multiplied by its number of dots
marks.add: the nine products are added to give 443

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step two, the sum. Multiply each value by its number of dots. This gives twenty eight, thirty, forty eight, eighty five and seventy two.
<bookmark mark='add'/>The rest are seventy six, sixty, twenty one and twenty three. Adding all nine gives four hundred and forty three.

marks.divide: 443 ÷ 25 = 17.72 is written beside the marker at 17

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step three, the mean. The sum is four hundred and forty three and the count is twenty five. Dividing gives seventeen point seven two.

marks.left: brackets from 17 to the dots at 14, 15 and 16 show 6, 4 and 3, total 13
marks.right: brackets from 17 to the dots at 18, 19, 20, 21 and 23 show 4, 8, 9, 4 and 6, total 31

beats.colours: left side blue, right side orange
narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step four, check by distances from seventeen. On the left, the dots are six, four and three away in all, which adds to thirteen.
<bookmark mark='right'/>On the right, the distances are four, eight, nine, four and six, which add to thirty one. Thirteen and thirty one are not equal.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>No, the mean is seventeen point seven two.
Seventeen does not balance the distances.
